title: Password reset by email link
description: Forgot-password flow for server apps: enumeration-safe reset requests, emailed one-time links with hashed 256-bit tokens, verify without consuming, single-use completion with a password policy, revocation of other links and sessions, a PostgreSQL store and a Fetch adapter.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build and Web Crypto (crypto.subtle, getRandomValues, randomUUID), TextEncoder/TextDecoder, btoa and the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral core; mount the HTTP adapter with your framework's catch-all route.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlPasswordResetStore with your query executor; on other databases implement PasswordResetStore with a unique token_hash and a single conditional consume.
Implement users.findByEmail(normalizedEmail) and users.setPasswordHash(userId, hash) against your user table.
Pass hashPassword from a maintained Argon2id, scrypt or bcrypt library, and a passwordPolicy that returns a list of problems (length, breached-password check).
Implement sendEmail with your email provider; set baseUrl to the absolute https URL of your reset form. Send the email from a queue if response timing must not reveal whether an account exists.
Pass revokeSessions(userId) to sign the user out everywhere after a reset.
Mount createPasswordResetHandler under one prefix with exact allowedOrigins, a rateLimit(key) hook and a trusted clientIp(request); log onRequestResult server-side.
limitations: Does not send email, hash passwords, store users or manage sessions; the application injects all four.

Response bodies are identical for known and unknown accounts, but request latency still includes the database insert and email send for known accounts; queue the email (sendEmail resolving after enqueue) if timing matters.
The email-binding check runs before the token is consumed; an email change in the instant between that check and the consume is not detected.
If users.setPasswordHash fails after the token was consumed, the link is spent and the user must request a new one.
Rate limiting is a hook only; back it with the rate-limit module or your gateway.

The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which runs as a single connection, not on every hosted Postgres or under real multi-connection contention.
Production database correctness, email deliverability, password hashing parameters and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: unknown, expired, used and revoked tokens all → 400 invalid-token (no 404 or 410)
token stored as SHA-256 hash and consumed once
completion revokes other links and calls revokeSessions; a link dies if the account email changes
options: ttlMs: link lifetime (default 30 min); maxActivePerUser: older links revoked (default 3)

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/password-reset.test.mjs tests/password-reset-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: request returns the identical result for known and unknown accounts; unknown accounts get no email and no stored token
the link carries a 256-bit base64url token and only its SHA-256 hash is stored
verify reports validity and expiry without consuming the token
complete sets the password hash once; replays, expired, unknown, malformed and revoked tokens fail identically with invalid-token
exactly one of four concurrent completes wins (memory store and PGlite)
a weak password is refused with its problems and leaves the token usable
a successful reset revokes the user's other pending links and calls revokeSessions
maxActivePerUser revokes the oldest links beyond the cap
a link stops working when the account email changes after the request
a failed email send revokes the new token and is reported only in the server-side serverError field
HTTP adapter: 202 with the same body for every request outcome, 200 verify, 204 complete, 400 invalid-token and weak-password with problems
HTTP adapter: origin check, 429 from the rateLimit hook keyed by IP and email, bounded body, cache-control no-store and referrer-policy no-referrer on all responses
schema.sql applies and the SQL store passes the core behaviors on PostgreSQL

changes: First release: core, in-memory store, PostgreSQL schema and store, and Fetch adapter.
